task_text: IKEA MuJoCo UPPSTÅ toy hammering block (IKEA UPPSTÅ toy hammering block (AA-2300462-4), all manual steps and the 8 pegs) with two 7-DoF Franka Panda arms, each with the MuJoCo Menagerie Panda hand (two-finger, tendon-coupled). Build the UPPSTÅ hammering block: set two dowels into one board end, press end block b onto them and drive screw b with the hex key; turn it over, set the other two dowels, press end block a on and drive screw a; stand the block on its feet and push the eight pegs into their holes. Success requirements: Both screws are seated and their seat welds engaged, each in its own hole within 0.6 mm along and across the hole axis, its axis within 2 degrees (spin free). Measured in the board frame against the scene's 'assembled' keyframe: both end blocks within 0.6 mm and 1 degree; every dowel position holds a dowel within 0.6 mm, its axis within 2 degrees (the four dowels are interchangeable). Every peg hole holds a peg (the eight are interchangeable) within 1 mm of the hole axis, its axis within 2 degrees, pushed down to the up position (at most 0.5 mm above it). The block stands on its feet (the board's assembled up direction within 1 degree of world +z) and no robot body touches any part at the end. The benchmark's terminal rules, the same in every IKEA MuJoCo task, come on top of these requirements. When your rows end: (1) the requirements above hold; (2) the parts are released: no robot link touches any part; (3) every part is at rest: at most 0.01 m/s and 0.05 rad/s; (4) the simulation never broke down: no non-finite state, no MuJoCo BADQACC / BADQPOS / BADQVEL warning, no contact of a part deeper than 10 mm, at any time. The grader then holds your last row for 1.0 s more and requires (1)-(4) again at its end. Mechanism: Each screw's coarse right-hand thread (2.5 mm pitch) runs in a helical thread in the board end: a screw advances only by being turned, by the hex key in its socket. Dowels and pegs hold by compliant flutes (spring-loaded slide joints, an interference fit) and friction. A screw's seat weld is armed once it is on its hole's axis within 3 mm of its seat; once its head touches and it has stopped relative to the board for 0.05 s, the screw and the end block it clamps are welded to the board at their current pose, and the screw and its hole's thread stop colliding. The scene's tick is 8 physics steps (2.5 ms); a row here is 4 of them (1.25 ms, 800 Hz).
